## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, thin, angular woman with a gaunt figure, sallow cheeks, and a face that eventually softens. Her dark hair, which shows gray streaks that increase over time, is always twisted behind her head into a hard little knot fastened aggressively with two wire hairpins. Standing side by side with [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), she is shorter than the girl.

## Personality

Marilla Cuthbert is a self-contained, sensible woman of narrow experience and rigid conscience. Though known to be sober and critical, she eventually mellows over time. When raising a child, she is fond of moralizing and prefers to keep a girl dressed in plain, dark dresses of an unvarying pattern. Beneath her strict demeanor, she has secretly harbored long-held critical thoughts about the local minister's sermons and prayers. Additionally, she possesses the skill to make celebrated three-year-old homemade currant wine.

## History

In her childhood, Marilla Cuthbert suffered from a painful remark made by an aunt about her plain appearance. In her youth, she had been sweethearts with John Blythe, but their relationship ended after she refused to forgive him following a quarrel. Marilla led an easy life at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) until she and her brother, [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md), arranged to adopt an orphan boy. Shocked when [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) brought home an orphan girl named [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) instead, Marilla initially insisted on returning her, but changed her mind after hearing Anne's tragic background and learning that a harsh local woman wanted her. Adopting [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), Marilla took on her religious and daily upbringing. Over time, Marilla grew deeply fond of [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) despite her frequent mishaps, such as accidentally serving currant wine to [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) or accidentally dyeing her hair green. When [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) fell from a roof, Marilla realized how much she truly loved her. Marilla supported Anne's education, allowing her to take advanced classes and attend Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy). Following Matthew's sudden death and news of her own failing eyesight, Marilla considered selling [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), but [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) gave up her college scholarship to remain home and care for her.

## Quotes

> "I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P25](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0025)

> “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VI. Marilla Makes Up Her Mind P35](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0035)

> "Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you. You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!"
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P2](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0002)

> "She’ll have her meals regular, and I’ll carry them up to her myself. But she’ll stay up there until she’s willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that’s final, Matthew."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P4](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0004)

> “I’ll go and have another look,” said Marilla, determining to be just. “If you put that brooch back it’s there still. If it isn’t I’ll know you didn’t, that’s all!”
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER XIV. Anne’s Confession P9](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0009)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla takes [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in as a foster mother after initially receiving her by mistake instead of the boy she and [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) requested. Although Marilla initially insists on returning [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), hearing the girl's difficult upbringing and refusing to let a harsh woman take her causes Marilla to change her mind and raise [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). Over time, Marilla oversees Anne's upbringing, discipline, and religious education, eventually coming to feel a warm surge of affection for the girl despite her theatrical nature.

### [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Marilla maintains a long-standing friendship with Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) despite their differing personalities. [Rachel](../character/rachel-lynde.md) frequently visits [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to share news or offer candid advice, such as warning Marilla against adoption or advising her on how to manage Anne's school strike. While Rachel's blunt demeanor sometimes sparks conflict—such as when she insults Anne's appearance—she remains a trusted neighbor and companion to Marilla.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P3](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P5](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0005), [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P12](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0012), +24 more_
